args.query: What does liquidation mean with leverage?

data.query: What does liquidation mean with leverage?

chunks.title: Leverage and liquidation
chunks.text: Leverage means using borrowed funds to take a position larger than one's own capital. With 10x leverage, a 1% price move changes the position's value by about 10% of the trader's margin. If losses reduce the margin below the exchange's maintenance requirement, the position is liquidated: the exchange closes it automatically. Large clusters of liquidations can accelerate price moves, because forced selling or buying adds to the move that triggered them.
